adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well then now."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Fire in the candle.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator lights the candle. 'Fire in the candle' is a static, unidiomatic noun phrase and does not express the action.

adjudicated.en: Open the diary.
comments: Wanted to make these flow, but they're CP'd in CCC4016 where it wouldn't work. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 今日起きたことを記していく。
adjudicated.en: I go record all that has happened today,
adjudicated.assessment: The progressive Japanese aspect does not license the nonidiomatic English sequence 'go record' without 'and' or an infinitive.

adjudicated.en: silently,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: detailed within the limits of the possible.
adjudicated.assessment: 可能な限り克明に means in as much detail as possible. The English uses an adjective without a governing noun and literalizes the limit phrase.

highlights.text: detailed within the limits of the possible

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: I promptly extinguish the candle.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: This time, there's the sound of light footsteps outside.
comments: See CCC3005, seems there was more sound last time. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: I lean out the window.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: ...it's Kiri.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 無人の街を足蹴にしていく。
adjudicated.en: Nonchalantly walking around this uninhabited city.
adjudicated.assessment: 街を足蹴にしていく evokes her treading or kicking her way across the deserted city. 'Nonchalantly walking around' removes the forceful physical image and adds an attitude.

adjudicated.jp: いずれにしても、やることは昨日と同じだろう。
adjudicated.en: In any event, what she's doing would be the same as yesterday.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 丑の刻参りさながら、太一人形は哀れ憎悪の対象に。
adjudicated.en: Just like in the ritual of Ushi no Koku Mairi, she makes the Taichi Doll into an object of pitiable hatred.
comments: http://ranmarelated.blogspot.it/2008/05/ushi-no-koku-mairi-japanese-voodoo.html - nothing to do with Ranma, but that's in English. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 見ても虚しいだけだろう。
adjudicated.en: Watching would be just pointless, I guess.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 前触れなく、背筋が冷え切った。
adjudicated.en: Without harbinger, my spine growing frozen.
adjudicated.assessment: The English lacks a finite main verb, and 'without harbinger' is not an idiomatic rendering of 'without warning.'

highlights.text: Without harbinger, my spine growing frozen.

adjudicated.jp: ぞわぞわと、脊髄を撫で上げられる感覚。
adjudicated.en: It's a hustling, bustling sensation that crawls up the spinal cord.
adjudicated.assessment: ぞわぞわ describes an eerie crawling or prickling sensation. 'Hustling, bustling' suggests busy cheerful activity and reverses the affect.

adjudicated.en: Fear creeping close like a ninja up to an enemy.
comments: Visuals. See CCB2011. Guess who it is! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 忍び寄る is an ordinary verb meaning to creep or steal closer. The English manufactures an explicit ninja simile and enemy absent from the source.

highlights.text: like a ninja up to an enemy

adjudicated.en: But that's just for a moment.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 嘘のように、悪寒は霧消してしまった。
adjudicated.en: Incredibly enough, the chill vanished in the fog.
comments: Can literally be read "it's almost a lie: the chill erased Kiri". Left odd. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 霧消 is a lexicalized word meaning dissipate or vanish completely. The English literalizes its characters as disappearance inside fog.

adjudicated.jp: 部屋の生ぬるさが戻り、じんわりと身を包む。
adjudicated.en: The room returning to half-hearted lukewarmth, I begin to dress myself.
adjudicated.assessment: The lukewarm air of the room returns and gently envelops his body. The English calls the warmth 'half-hearted' and changes the room's enveloping action into Taichi beginning to dress himself.

highlights.text: The room returning to half-hearted lukewarmth, I begin to dress myself.

adjudicated.en: And now... I,
adjudicated.assessment: 今の……は is a broken question meaning 'What was that just now?' The English instead begins a first-person clause and leaves it unfinished.
